source.chapter_title: Dasas of the several Bhava-lords and their Bhuktis

notes: Slokas 2-13 give the dasha of each house lord when strong; 15-20 when weak. Sloka 14 defines strong as retrograde, in its own, exalted or friendly sign and outside the 6th, 8th and 12th; weak as in an enemy's or debilitation sign, combust, or in the 6th, 8th or 12th. A planet ruling two houses gives the results of both. Slokas 43-44 say these results also show in sub-periods, so each rule is applied to the sub-period lord as well.

skipped.reason: Assign each planet's general significations to its dasha: guidance, not a rule.
Need nakshatra-based sub-period lords or inter-planet enmity tests not yet encoded.
Timing of death: excluded by policy.
Dasha results modified by current transits and the Moon's daily position: not yet encoded.
Functional benefic/malefic and yogakaraka principles: already covered by BPHS ch. 36 and the raja-yoga rules.
Rising/descending dasha classes: need the planet's distance from exaltation.

rules.text: Dasha of the 1st lord, well placed: rise to eminence, a settled and happy life, physical strength, a bright presence, and prosperity growing steadily like the waxing Moon.
Dasha of the 1st lord, weak or badly placed: fear and anxiety, a change or loss of work and position, and a low profile.
Dasha of the 2nd lord, well placed: additions to the family, good food, earnings from speaking or teaching, and eloquence that wins an audience's approval.
Dasha of the 2nd lord, weak or badly placed: poor showing in public, broken promises, unwelcome news, harsh words, heavy spending and worry about authority.
Dasha of the 3rd lord, well placed: friendship and help from siblings, good news, chances to show courage, leadership, honour, and praise for one's qualities.
Dasha of the 3rd lord, weak or badly placed: bad advice in one's undertakings, trouble from hidden rivals, humiliation and a blow to pride.
Dasha of the 4th lord, well placed: help to relatives, success in farming or land, vehicles, new land or a new house, wealth and promotion.
Dasha of the 4th lord, weak or badly placed: worry for the mother, illness among close friends, and risks to land and house.
Dasha of the 5th lord, well placed: the birth of a child, respect and good times with relatives, or an advisory post with those in power.
Dasha of the 5th lord, weak or badly placed: worry over children, confused thinking, deception, tiring travel and displeasure of authority.
Dasha of the 6th lord, well placed: opponents overcome through bold action, good health, generosity, power and prosperity.
Dasha of the 6th lord, weak or badly placed: theft, reverses and defeat, servile work, and being criticised or scandalised.
Dasha of the 7th lord, well placed: new clothes and comforts, contentment and happiness with one's partner, a wedding or celebration in the family, and pleasure trips.
Dasha of the 7th lord, weak or badly placed: separation from a partner, trouble through relationships, and much wandering.
Dasha of the 8th lord, well placed: debts fully cleared, a rise in position, quarrels ending, and gains of livestock and helpers.
Dasha of the 8th lord, weak or badly placed: deep sorrow, poor judgement, jealousy, poverty, fruitless travel, slander and humiliation.
Dasha of the 9th lord, well placed: lasting prosperity, happiness and wealth with spouse, children and family, good deeds, official favour and devotion.
Dasha of the 9th lord, weak or badly placed: a sense of divine displeasure, trouble for spouse and children, wrong actions and financial hardship.
Dasha of the 10th lord, well placed: undertakings brought to success, a happy life, wide renown, a permanent position, good and proper work done cleverly, and great respect.
Dasha of the 10th lord, weak or badly placed: efforts that bear no fruit, loss of honour, poor conduct, time spent away in foreign places and general trouble.
Dasha of the 11th lord, well placed: an uninterrupted flow of money, reunions with family, people in one's service, domestic happiness and great prosperity.
Dasha of the 11th lord, weak or badly placed: bad news, worry over a sibling or the children's health, misery and deception.
Dasha of the 12th lord, well placed: generous spending on good causes, meritorious acts that offset past wrongs, and official honours.
Dasha of the 12th lord, weak or badly placed: dishonour, restriction, and wealth draining away like the waning Moon.

variants.text: The sub-period lord is in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the dasha lord: an unhappy sub-period, colouring the matters of the house it occupies.
The sub-period lord is well placed from the dasha lord: a good sub-period for the matters of the house it occupies.

rules.text: Both the dasha lord and the sub-period lord rule or occupy the 6th, 8th or 12th: an unfavourable sub-period.
Mars exalted in the 10th or 11th: during its dasha, rivals are overcome and one rises to wide authority and renown, providing for many.
Venus in its own or exalted sign in the 10th, 11th or 12th, unafflicted: during its dasha, gems and precious things, a broadened mind, great affluence and wide praise.
One of the dasha and sub-period lords rules a trine and the other an angle: they support each other and the sub-period is good, even if they are not otherwise connected.
